title: Video Editor Intern
summary: Learn to cut short-form social video for real clients — hooks, pacing, sound and polish — alongside our editors.
intro: Peak Exposure Media is a video-first content marketing agency in Provo, Utah. We make cinematic social content for premium brands in home building, design and lifestyle, and we act as the outsourced marketing department for most of our clients. We're looking for a Video Editor Intern to cut real client work alongside our editors.

This is an unpaid, in-person internship: 5–10 hours a week minimum (more if you want it), any start date, one semester or longer. You'll get full access to our gear and office, a stipend for travel to client locations, and lunch on us at team meetings. If you need it for school credit, we'll sign whatever your program needs.

Here's the honest deal. You'll own one real, recurring piece of client work for the whole semester and get good at it, with our team coaching you along the way. That might be cutting Reels from footage our videographers shoot, captions and cover frames, organizing and logging footage, or a recurring series for one client. You don't need to be great yet. You do need a baseline — this isn't a start-from-zero program — and you need to care about getting better.
We hire for four things: creative bravery, excellence over easy, client obsession and an ownership mentality. Interns too.
processNote: Two steps, both before an interview: a short application and a short written assessment. No test project. We reply to everyone within 24 hours of each step.

values.name: Excellence Over Easy
values.desc: Quality matters; don't rush or choose the easy route.

values.name: Client-Obsessed
values.desc: Care deeply about the client's results, not just completing deliverables.

values.name: Ownership Mentality
values.desc: Act like it's your company, not just a job.

assessment.title: Written Assessment
assessment.blurb: About 20 minutes. Four short questions, 100 words each. No editing required.

questions.prompt: Watch the first three seconds of any Reel you think has a great hook (link it). What exactly makes it work — visually, in the audio, in the text?
questions.strong: Breaks the hook into parts: the first frame, motion, text on screen, the sound, the promise it makes. Red flag: 'it grabs attention' with no mechanics.

questions.prompt: You're handed 40 minutes of raw footage from a custom home tour — walkthrough shots, detail shots, the builder talking. Walk us through how you'd turn it into a 30-second Reel, step by step.
questions.strong: Has a process: watch it all and mark selects, find the story or the single best moment, lock the hook, cut to music, then polish. Mentions sound and the first 3 seconds. Red flag: 'pick the best clips and put them together.'

questions.prompt: Our videographer shot it beautifully, but the builder's on-camera audio has an AC hum and he rambles. What do you do?
questions.strong: Tries to fix it (noise reduction, cut around it, music under it, use the best line only, captions), knows when to flag it instead of hiding it, and protects the client from a bad result. Red flag: 'I'd just use it' or giving up.

questions.prompt: A client comes back with: "Love it, but can it feel more high-end?" Nothing else. What changes would you try, and what would you ask them?
questions.strong: Translates vague feedback into concrete moves (slower pacing, fewer cuts, restrained music, cleaner type, let shots breathe, color) and asks one or two sharp questions with references. Red flag: adds more effects.
